# Task — define the work that is ready to execute

Read `references/workspace-records.md` and `references/record-interface.md` before
writing. Resolve the project's records and repository, then reuse the existing task
or live legacy work item for the same outcome. Follow the established format for
unmapped projects. The record interface supplies the Task template.

Use the existing project record and settled conversation first. Recover factual
gaps from available evidence. For each
deliverable, carry forward the elicit decision and the reason that constrains
it, the specific interaction agreed in the mockup, and the probe result within
the limits of what was tested. Use whichever sources exist. Link to the relevant
decision, mockup state, or probe finding beside the item when it helps the reader
understand the requirement. Keep any untested outcome visible as pending.

Use a representative acceptance example to make the agreed experience legible
to the user and the implementer. If two plausible readings of the sources would
produce different user-visible results or acceptance criteria, show the concrete
difference and ask the user which applies. Continue directly when the decision
is already clear. An unresolved item can stay open while independent, authorized
items remain ready.

State the goal and boundary. Pair each independently verifiable deliverable with
its acceptance check in the same list: entry or starting state, action, and
observable result. Preserve affected existing behavior. Include older saved data,
failure/retry, and continuation paths when the outcome depends on them. For a
generated answer, specify what the answer must demonstrate from the source.
A small task may need one checkbox. Split records only when work must be owned,
scheduled, or closed independently.

Add a brief decision and reason under a deliverable when it changes what counts
as success. A term lookup illustrates the format.

- [ ] Let readers look up a term and resume reading at the same place.
  - Keep the definition next to the selected term so readers can retain their place.
  - Accept when selecting the same term in two different contexts shows the
    meaning for each passage, and dismissing the card leaves the passage in place.

Describe the promised result and evidence. Leave module placement, implementation
sequence, API design, and test mechanisms to engineering. Initialize or preserve
the whole task's status independently of the checklist. When updating, retain
verified progress and keep the next ready action and any material blockers visible.

Report the task and its next action. Recording work leaves it planned until
execution is authorized. When the request already includes implementation,
continue the ready items with nav-do discipline under that same authority.
